test_title: SSC Selection Post Matric Level Official Paper (Held on: 2 Feb 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: The average weight of a class of 20 students is 44 kg. A new student joins the class the average weight decreases by 300 gm. What is the weight of the new student (in kg)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Weight of new student = Old Average − (New Total Students × Decrease in Average)

Decrease in Average = 300 gm = 0.3 kg

New Total Students = 20 + 1 = 21

Weight = 44 − (21 × 0.3)

Weight = 44 − 6.3 = 37.7 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 37.7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of students initially (n₁) = 20

Initial average weight (A₁) = 44 kg

Decrease in average = 300 gm = 0.3 kg

**Formula:**

Total Weight = Number of students × Average Weight

 
 Initial Group (20)
 Avg = 44 kg
 
 Final Group (21)
 Avg = 43.7 kg
 

 New student weight = Total₂₁ − Total₂₀
 Result: 917.7 − 880 = 37.7 kg

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total weight of 20 students = 20 × 44 = 880 kg

⇒ New average weight = 44 − 0.3 = 43.7 kg

⇒ New total number of students = 21

⇒ Total weight of 21 students = 21 × 43.7 = 917.7 kg

⇒ Weight of the new student = 917.7 − 880 = 37.7 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 37.7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effect of Adding a Member

If the average increases, the new member's weight = Old Average + (New Total × Increase). If it decreases, use − instead of +.

Net Deviation Principle

The sum of deviations from the average is always zero. New student weight = Old Average + Total Members × Change in Average.

Unit Conversion

Always ensure units are uniform: 1 kg = 1000 gm. Thus, 300 gm = 300/1000 = 0.3 kg.</p
